narrative:
Your application was rejected because the model estimated a 54.6% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That means, based on the information reviewed, failure was judged slightly more likely than passing, so the application did not clear the admission threshold.

The strongest factor driving this prediction was your third-year class standing. You were in the second decile, well below the average of about the sixth decile among students who were accepted. Because this was the most influential feature, it was the main reason the prediction leaned toward failure.

Your undergraduate GPA of 2.60, compared with an accepted-student average of 3.23, was the second most influential factor, but in your profile it actually pushed the prediction toward passing rather than failure. Family income was the third most influential factor; your high-income bracket also pushed slightly toward passing, though less strongly than GPA. These positive factors were not enough to offset the third-year standing signal.

Your gender and race were not used in the prediction. To improve a future application, focus on strengthening the areas that carry the most weight: raise your academic standing if possible, consider retaking the LSAT—your 32 is below the accepted average of 37.18—and seek admissions advising. You may also ask whether additional context or a delayed application with stronger credentials would help.
